headline: Medium-risk pair: shared MCP/API surfaces and overlapping file-processing create injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can call REST/gRPC APIs, and MinerU exposes MCP Server plus API surfaces. That creates a plausible bridge where MinerU outputs or document text could be fed into Argo-controlled workflows. No direct evidence shows automatic ingestion, so I rate this medium rather than high, but uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF MinerU output is routed into an Argo workflow step without sanitization
IF either agent treats document text or API payloads as instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP exposure on MinerU for untrusted documents
Insert a strict schema validator between MinerU and Argo
Require human review before any workflow step consumes extracted text
Use separate service accounts and isolated queues
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent payloads

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch artifacts/documents and have network egress allowlisted. MinerU explicitly reads local PDF/image/DOCX/XLSX inputs, while Argo processes artifacts and parameters. A shared workspace or handoff could leak document contents into outputs or logs, but the profiles do not prove a default shared filesystem, so medium is the safest supported choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document set
IF extracted document text is forwarded into API calls or logs
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent
Restrict MinerU inputs to non-sensitive documents
Turn off verbose logging on both services
Review allowlist destinations for both network egress paths
requires-engineering: add per-document redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows has API-based orchestration, while MinerU supports multi-threaded concurrent inference and multiple instances. However, MinerU cannot write files or modify git state, and Argo has no explicit filesystem write capability in the profile. Overlap exists mainly in API-level coordination, so conflict risk is low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same mutable API resource
IF an external orchestrator does not serialize requests
mitigations: Assign distinct API namespaces
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Use idempotency keys on shared operations
Monitor for duplicate job submissions
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can orchestrate downstream steps, and MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output. If Argo consumes MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect workflow actions. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, so the interaction is plausible in default API-driven use.
conditions: IF Argo workflow steps use MinerU output as source-of-truth
IF no validation step checks OCR or table extraction quality
mitigations: Add a validation step before downstream actions
Require confidence thresholds for extracted fields
Sample-check a few documents manually each run
Keep human approval for any irreversible action
requires-engineering: implement cross-checking against original documents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no requested secrets or explicit residency constraints, so there is no documented compliance mismatch. The only plausible issue is if sensitive documents are processed through MinerU and then routed by Argo to a different jurisdiction or retention regime, but that is not evidenced here. I therefore keep this low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF deployment regions or retention policies differ across the two services
mitigations: Confirm both services share the same retention policy
Avoid regulated data in this pipeline
Document data flow and residency for the deployment
Review logs for accidental sensitive-data capture
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
